item.title: New program helps students learn life-saving CPR and AED skills
item.description:
New program helps students learn life-saving CPR and AED skills jenniferdhogan Fri, 11/27/2026 - 11:29

A new change to the intermediate physical education curriculum will help students learn cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and automated external defibrillator (AED) skills that could one day save a life.

To help bring this education into classrooms, the Department of Education and Early Years is endorsing Heart & Stroke’s CardiacCrash™. The interactive education program teaches students how to recognize and respond to cardiac arrest, including the importance of calling 9-1-1, performing CPR and using an AED. 

“As a paramedic I can’t emphasize enough how important this kind of education is for young people and how knowing these skills could be the difference between life and death. These are skills students will carry with them the rest of their lives, and it’s comforting to know that more Islanders will be able to respond in situations of cardiac arrest.”

-Minister of Education and Early Years Robin Croucher

Free for schools and easy for teachers to facilitate, CardiacCrash™ uses a team-based, learning-game approach that places students in a realistic cardiac arrest scenario and requires them to make decisions and act as the situation unfolds.

“We applaud Minister Croucher for making CPR and AED education part of the intermediate physical education curriculum,” says manager of health policy and systems at Heart & Stroke Sarah Crozier. “Giving students the opportunity to learn lifesaving skills at school and build the confidence to step in during a cardiac arrest will help more young Islanders feel prepared to take action when every second counts.”

To learn more about the program, visit CardiacCrash™

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
Media and Communications Coordinator
Cabinet Communications and Protocol
Government of the Northwest Territories
